task_instance: Build and run an LLM-as-judge evaluation pipeline per SKILL.md: (1) pairwise comparison of two candidate answers to 'Explain how neural networks learn to a complete beginner' with mandatory position-swap bias mitigation and confidence calibration, (2) direct scoring with evidence-first justification of a factual-accuracy claim, (3) rubric generation for a 'Code Readability' criterion, (4) metric validation (Cohen's kappa, Spearman's rho) for judge-vs-human agreement. The judging itself was performed by the acting agent (the LLM in this session) applying the skill's prompt structures and criteria directly -- exactly how this skill is meant to be invoked -- while a deterministic Python layer implements the bias-mitigation algorithm, rubric templating, and statistics the skill specifies.
evidence: Work directory: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/muratcankoylan__agent-skills-for-context-engineering__advanced-evaluation@offline-workstation . Files: inputs.json (task specs), judge_raw_outputs.json (two independent pairwise judgments, A-first and B-first, produced by genuinely re-evaluating clarity/accessibility per pass), direct_scoring_raw.json (evidence-first factual-accuracy judgment catching that the sample response wrongly names Sydney instead of Canberra as Australia's capital, correctly scoring 1/5 despite confident tone -- demonstrating authority-bias resistance), pipeline.py (implements SKILL.md's 5-step pairwise algorithm: position mapping, per-criterion consistency check, final verdict with averaged confidence or TIE-on-disagreement; a rubric generator producing 5 calibrated levels + edge cases for 'Code Readability'; and metric validation via scipy/sklearn), evaluation_output.json (full run output). Ran `python3 pipeline.py` -> stdout 'ALL CHECKS PASSED' plus summary: pairwise_final_winner=B, pairwise_confidence=0.875 (avg of 0.9 and 0.85, both passes agreed after the position swap, verifying the bias-mitigation logic runs correctly and matches the skill's confidence-calibration formula), direct_score=1 (evidence-based, catches the factual error), rubric_levels=5 (matches 1-5 scale), spearman_rho=0.8715 and cohens_kappa=0.6104 (sklearn) which exactly matched a hand-coded kappa implementation (assert in pipeline.py), validating the Metric Selection Framework's ordinal-scale metrics. All 7 in-script assertions passed with no exceptions. No network access, package installs, or MCP/connector tools were used or needed -- everything ran with already-installed python3, numpy, scipy, and scikit-learn.
note: The one nuance worth flagging: this skill's 'core deliverable' (an LLM judging text) is inherently performed by whichever LLM/agent is running the skill -- there is no separate network LLM API to call, and none was needed. That is consistent with how the skill is designed to be used (as agent instructions for prompt structure, bias mitigation, and rubric design), so no blocker applies here.
